headline: Students block Dhaka road demanding principal's resignation
summary: Students of Government College of Applied Human Science protested on Friday, blocking Azimpur Road after alleging police baton-charged them during a rescue operation.
details: Students of Government College of Applied Human Science, formerly Home Economics College, blocked both sides of Azimpur Road on Friday morning to demand the removal of Principal Prof Meherun Nessa.
The protest follows a Thursday night incident where students claim police baton-charged them while rescuing the principal, who had been confined to her office by protesters.
Lalbagh Division Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohammad Mostak Sarker denied the baton-charge allegations, stating that only female officers were deployed to rescue the principal safely.
The conflict began when students protested the cancellation of residential seats for two students and a demand for Tk 12,500 in auditorium usage fees following a minor incident.
Principal Prof Meherun Nessa defended the charges, stating the students had used the college auditorium from 10am to 5am and must pay for the electricity used.
Students have announced an indefinite suspension of all campus activities until the principal resigns in writing and action is taken against the involved police officers.
caption:
Students block Dhaka road after alleging police baton-charge during a campus standoff.

Students of Government College of Applied Human Science, formerly Home Economics College, blocked both sides of Azimpur Road on Friday morning to demand the removal of Principal Prof Meherun Nessa.

The protest follows a Thursday night incident where students claim police baton-charged them while rescuing the principal, who had been confined to her office by protesters.

Lalbagh Division Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohammad Mostak Sarker denied the baton-charge allegations, stating that only female officers were deployed to rescue the principal safely.

The conflict began when students protested the cancellation of residential seats for two students and a demand for Tk 12,500 in auditorium usage fees following a minor incident.

Principal Prof Meherun Nessa defended the charges, stating the students had used the college auditorium from 10am to 5am and must pay for the electricity used.

Students have announced an indefinite suspension of all campus activities until the principal resigns in writing and action is taken against the involved police officers.

headline_marked: 6 for 90: [[Hasan Mahmud claims career-best figures]] in Sylhet Test
headline: 6 for 90: Hasan Mahmud claims career-best figures in Sylhet Test
summary: Pacer Hasan Mahmud led Bangladesh's fightback, securing his fifth Test five-wicket haul and first on home soil to bowl out West Indies for 356.
details: Bangladesh completed a strong fightback against West Indies on day two of the Sylhet Test, bowling out the visitors for 356 shortly after lunch.
Pacer Hasan Mahmud was the star of the day, finishing with career-best figures of six for 90 from 24 overs.
Hasan's dominant spell included dismissing overnight centurion Aamir Jangoo (133) and Roston Chase in consecutive deliveries, nearly achieving a hat-trick.
This marks Hasan's fifth Test five-wicket haul overall and his first five-wicket haul on home soil.
Mehidy Hasan Miraz also contributed with two wickets for 82 runs, while Taskin Ahmed claimed two wickets to wrap up the innings.
West Indies, who resumed on 235 for four, lost their remaining six wickets for just 121 runs in 106.4 overs.
caption:
6 wickets for 90 runs! Hasan Mahmud delivers a career-best performance to dismantle the West Indies.

Bangladesh completed a strong fightback against West Indies on day two of the Sylhet Test, bowling out the visitors for 356 shortly after lunch.

Pacer Hasan Mahmud was the star of the day, finishing with career-best figures of six for 90 from 24 overs.

Hasan's dominant spell included dismissing overnight centurion Aamir Jangoo (133) and Roston Chase in consecutive deliveries, nearly achieving a hat-trick.

This marks Hasan's fifth Test five-wicket haul overall and his first five-wicket haul on home soil.

Mehidy Hasan Miraz also contributed with two wickets for 82 runs, while Taskin Ahmed claimed two wickets to wrap up the innings.

West Indies, who resumed on 235 for four, lost their remaining six wickets for just 121 runs in 106.4 overs.
